description:
Files:
- crate-jmap-chat-client/src/methods/blob.rs:176-177 (public doc references the constant)
- crate-jmap-chat-client/src/methods/mod.rs:195 (constant is `pub(crate)`)

`blob_convert`'s rustdoc contains:
```
/// `response.created[CALL_ID]`.  On failure the error is in
/// `response.not_created[CALL_ID]`.
```

`CALL_ID` is declared `pub(crate) const CALL_ID: &str = "r1"`. External callers cannot import or read this constant. They are told to index into a HashMap using a key they cannot see.

In practice today the key is `"r1"`, hardcoded — so callers who read the source can recover the value. But:
- The doc is misleading as written: an external caller types `let result = response.created[jmap_chat_client::methods::CALL_ID];` and gets a private-item error.
- A future internal refactor that changes `CALL_ID` (e.g. to UUIDs per request) silently breaks every external caller who hardcoded `"r1"` instead of the constant.

Two fixes, pick one:
1. **Expose the constant**: change to `pub const CALL_ID: &str = "r1";`. Now callers can write `response.created[jmap_chat_client::methods::CALL_ID]` and the doc is honest.
2. **Wrap the access**: change `blob_convert` to return the inner value directly (`Result<Option<BlobObject>, ClientError>` instead of `Result<SetResponse, ClientError>`), eliminating the index-the-map step entirely.

Option 2 is the cleaner caller experience and matches what `message_create` does. Option 1 is the minimum fix.

Note: this also affects every other method that returns `SetResponse` and tells the caller to index into `created[CALL_ID]` — applies to roughly every `*_create` method. The audit only spot-checked `blob_convert` explicitly, but the same docstring pattern recurs in `chat.rs`, `space.rs`, `message.rs`, `misc.rs`. A workspace-wide pattern decision is needed.
title: CALL_ID referenced in public blob_convert doc but is pub(crate)
